statement0:
The word "less" is mentioned two or more times in 12.5% of neuroscience papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "less" , 34.6% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a lower than the typical Psychology paper (median shown for reference); relative to other words, papers with "less" are in the bottom 38th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better). Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability(see Supplemental Materials 7.3 of the associated paper).
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "less" tend to be published in lower impact factor journals (21st percentile among all words) but tend to be cited more (66th percentile word). In general, this word is negatively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are less likely to publish papers containing "less" (37th percentile).
